guide.title: Symbolic full-domain model counting
guide.summary: exact model counts and weighted model counts over a declared assignment universe (never observed rows): BOOL-001 predicates compiled to reduced ordered decision diagrams under a variable order within node and step budgets (TRUE / FALSE / UNKNOWN classes, rational literal weights, lexicographic witnesses), finite-domain factor systems with dependent weight and constraint tables by variable elimination within a width budget, a native brute-force verifier, and a bounded Shannon expansion returning certified bounds instead of an extrapolation.

COUNT-002.cpu: Native C (math_symcount.c, the exact L-limb arithmetic and the count functions inline in math_symcount.h): a decision-diagram builder (hash-consed reduced ordered BDD nodes over a declared order, iterative Shannon apply for AND / OR / XOR with a lossy computed table, node / apply-step / byte budgets checked at every growth and refused at the first node past the limit) and its immutable diagrams renumbered from the deepest level; BOOL-001 programs over k <= 64 variables compiled two-valued (one root) or three-valued (the TRUE and FALSE indicator functions under Kleene's connectives) under the natural, a given or the DFS first-appearance order; exact model counts and weighted model counts over the whole 2^k assignment universe (rational literal weights scaled to integers over per-variable common denominators, counts in L 64-bit limbs with the bound prod (a + b) < 2^(64 L) proven before counting, reduced to canonical rationals with FND-009 big integers), TRUE + FALSE + UNKNOWN = TOTAL; the first m TRUE or FALSE assignments in lexicographic order of the levels; a brute-force enumeration of the 2^k assignments (64 per word with BOOL-001's evaluator) for verification; a breadth-first bounded Shannon expansion with possible-value sets whose open branches give certified lower and upper bounds per class (exact when none is open); finite-domain factor systems (domains <= 2^16, scopes <= 31 variables, nonnegative rational tables scaled per factor, zeros as hard constraints) counted by variable elimination under a given, min-fill or min-degree order with the width (the largest joint table) checked first and its exact need reported, model counting by indicators, witnesses decoded without backtracking in lexicographic order of the reverse elimination order, and a factor brute force. Every result is labelled as a count of the declared assignment universe, distinct from COUNT-001's observed rows.
COUNT-002.gpu: CUDA kernels math_symcount_gpu.cu: tr_mgpu_symcount_levels counts a compiled diagram with one launch per level from the deepest, one work item per node writing its exact L-limb weighted count into its own slot from its children's (the shared tr_symc_node_count, the skipped levels' weight sums multiplied in), then one work item per root; tr_mgpu_symcount_brute enumerates the 2^k assignments in work items over slices of 64-point words (BOOL-001's word evaluator, popcounts of the TRUE / FALSE / UNKNOWN words, the weights of the TRUE and FALSE assignments as H(word) times the low variables' weights) with local sums added by one 64-bit atomic per count and a multi-word atomic add per L-limb sum (exact modulo 2^(64 L), exact by the host's bound). The readbacks are adopted natively after consistency checks (tr_symc_dd_adopt, tr_symc_brute_adopt); raw words equal the CPU's bit for bit.
budgets: Compilation: variables = k (programs), circuit = every node the builder holds (a refusal names the first node past the limit), iterations = Shannon apply steps, bytes = the node, unique-table, computed-table and stack arrays at every growth.
Counts: circuit = diagram nodes, output = roots, bytes = nodes x L x 8 (CUDA: every device copy, the node values and the widest level's scratch); witnesses: output = m.

Brute force: variables = k, support = 2^k, circuit = program nodes, bytes (CUDA: per work item node words and sums); bounded search: iterations = max_evaluations (exact or certified bounds, never refused for a larger space), bytes = the branch queue.

Factors: variables = n, support = entries, tensor = the largest table; elimination: tensor = the width (exact need), iterations = the products, bytes = every message at L limbs per entry, output = 2 + witnesses; factor brute force: support = prod d_i.
limitations: Programs over at most 64 variables (63 for the brute force); no complement edges, dynamic reordering or garbage collection inside one compilation: the node budget counts every node held, and the order is given or the DFS heuristic.

Weights are nonnegative exact rationals with int64 numerators and denominators (scaled per variable or factor below 2^126); a formula with dependent weights is counted as a factor system (CNF clauses as 0/1 tables), not as a weighted diagram.

The bounded search is breadth first in a fixed order without caching of equal residual formulas: its certified bounds can be loose; variable elimination, search and witness decoding run single-threaded on the CPU (the level count and the brute force have kernels).
Counts are of the declared universe only; statements about observed rows remain COUNT-001's certificates (no FND-007 certificate is emitted for a symbolic count).
